title: Towards Interpretable Visual Decoding with Attention to Brain Representations
claim: Prior decoders route signals through intermediate feature spaces in two stages; ours conditions the generator directly, enabling interpretability probing.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, left-to-right; two-stage loop versus end-to-end plus probing row
description: A wide figure split by a vertical dashed line into 'Prior Work' on the left and 'Our Work' on the right. The left panel shows a two-stage loop. Stage 1 goes from stimuli icon to brain icon, then a curved gray arrow leads into a blue wireframe sphere of colored clusters labeled 'Brain-Foundation Model Aligned Feature Space'. Stage 2 goes from that space to an image generator (palette in a green trapezoid) and then to decoded stimuli. The right panel has a top row, 'End-to-End Decoding': stimuli, brain data, image generator, decoded stimuli, joined by gray block arrows. Below it, 'Interpretability Probing' links a curved arrow from the generator to attention-weight heatmaps, a brain surface flatmap, and an ROI attention map overlaid on a giraffe photo. The eye goes first to the bold titles and the colorful brain icons.
caption: Overview. Left: Typical two-stage decoding pipelines first map brain activity to intermediate feature spaces (e.g., CLIP/DINO) and then use those embeddings to guide a generative model. Right: Our end-to-end approach conditions a latent diffusion model directly on brain activity, enabling interpretations of the generative dynamics in both image and brain spaces.
abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that complex visual stimuli can be decoded from human brain activity using deep generative models, offering new ways to probe how the brain represents real-world scenes. However, many existing approaches first map brain signals into intermediate image or text feature spaces before guiding the generative process, which obscures the contributions of different brain areas to the final reconstruction output. In this work, we propose NeuroAdapter, a visual decoding framework that directly conditions a latent diffusion model on brain representations, bypassing the need for intermediate feature spaces. Our method demonstrates competitive visual reconstruction quality on public fMRI datasets compared to prior work, while providing greater transparency into how brain signals drive visual reconstruction. To this end, we introduce an Image-Brain BI-directional interpretability framework (IBBI) that analyzes cross-attention patterns across diffusion denoising steps to reveal how different cortical areas influence the unfolding generative trajectory. Our work highlights the potential of end-to-end brain-to-image reconstruction and establishes a path for interpretable neural decoding.
